description.value: A randomized trial examining whether two weeks of playing an empathy-training video game, Crystals of Kaydor, changes empathic accuracy, empathy-related BOLD activation, and resting-state functional connectivity in adolescents compared with the active control game Bastion.

spans.text: Participants completed a resting state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) scan and an EA task during an fMRI scan before and after 2 weeks of daily gameplay with either the empathy training game, Crystals (  N   = 34), or the commercial video game Bastion (  N   = 40), an active control condition.

value: We hypothesized that participants who played the empathy training game Crystals would show greater empathic accuracy on a behavioral task, and higher self-reported empathic concern following training
We predicted that increased empathic accuracy would be associated with greater empathic concern.

we predicted that increases in empathic accuracy should be accompanied by, and related to, increased activation during the empathic accuracy task and increased resting connectivity for the neural regions underlying empathic accuracy in adolescents, including VMPFC, DMPFC and RTPJ.
we expected that training adolescents to more accurately empathize would be supported and reflected by strengthened connectivity wihin this network.

we expected that participants with greater engagement with and performance on the empathy training game mechanics (as measured by telemetry data collected from the game) would show the most change in empathic accuracy and related brain activation.

description.value: Participants rated the emotions of video targets, their own emotions, or target eye gaze.

stimuli.value: Videos of targets describing emotional events from their adolescence.

description.value: Participants rated the target's emotion in the video from negative to positive, matching the target's own ratings; this was the empathic accuracy condition and required continuous emotional-state judgments.
Participants rated their own emotion while watching the video from negative to positive using the same 1–9 scale; this required self-referential emotional judgments.
Participants rated the direction of the target's eye gaze from left to right on a 1–9 scale; this was a control condition requiring gaze-direction judgments.

instructions.value: For OTHER trials, rate the target's emotion in the video from negative to positive exactly as the target rated themselves. For SELF trials, rate your own emotion from negative to positive. For GAZE trials, rate the direction of the target's eye gaze from left to right.

value: Empathic accuracy calculated as the Fisher r-to-Z transformed correlation between target and perceiver rating time courses for each video
Ratings collected on a 1–9 Likert scale
18 trials per scan: 6 OTHER, 6 SELF, and 6 GAZE
One trial excluded because of large disagreement between target and perceiver ratings

spans.text: Resting state fMRI connectivity was assessed based on the Fisher Z normalized correlation between each of the seeds and each of the target ROIs (or for each voxel in the voxel-wise analysis).

Three functional scan runs were acquired for the empathic accuracy paradigm using a gradient echo EPI sequence (64 × 64 in-plane resolution, 220 mm FOV, TR/TE/Flip = 2000ms/20 ms/60°, 36 × 4.5 mm), and one resting state functional MRI run was acquired with 264 time points using the same EPI sequence.
Images were acquired on a GE X750-3.0 Tesla MRI scanner (Waukesha, WI) with a 32-channel head coil (Nova Medical Inc., Wilmington, MA).
